Nora (People Ops): quick thread to capture a couple follow-ups from today's all-hands Q&A about onboarding promises, transfers, and calibration timelines. dropping the answers here so managers and recruiters have a single reference. :thread:
Diego (Eng): thanks! first: if a hiring manager promises a promotion at 6 months in the offer call, is that binding or just guidance?
Nora (People Ops): it's a commitment but not an automatic comp bump. we ask managers to document the onboarding promo plan in the offer notes and submit a promotion packet at the agreed time. People Ops will track but approval follows normal calibration.
Priya (EM): where should managers record the plan? Greenhouse? a google doc?
Nora (People Ops): Greenhouse -> Offer Notes is preferred for audit trail + attach the 1-paragraph onboarding promo plan. i'll paste a copyable snippet below.
Sam (IC): can we see that snippet here? helps when managers forget the wording live on calls.
Nora (People Ops): sure — copy this into offers:
"Onboarding promotion plan: target review at 6 months; measurable goals attached; manager and peer reviewer named; promotion contingent on calibration and budget approval."
kate-recruiting: noted. i'll update the offer playbook and use that exact phrase to reduce negotiation back-and-forth.
payroll-bot: FYI: salary changes are effective on the first payroll after HR approval (no retro-pay by default). Exceptions require finance sign-off.
Diego (Eng): transfer case: if someone moves teams mid-cycle, do they keep original review date?
Nora (People Ops): yes by default. if new role materially changes scope, new manager can request a transfer recalibration. both managers + People Ops must sign off.
Sam (IC): appeals timeline? some folks were confused during live Q&A.
Nora (People Ops): appeals accepted for 14 days after calibration email. managers file packets for direct reports; ICs talk to their manager first. we'll publish a small flowchart and link when the handbook update lands next week. :calendar:
